scope: Real record of the Codex desktop session that produced this commit. Student turns are quoted verbatim. Agent turns and tool results are summarised from the session; numbers are copied from actual command output.
redaction: No secrets. Local absolute paths shortened to repository-relative paths.
completeness_note: In this session the student gave the task and two short steering messages. Design, implementation and experiments below were proposed and run by the Agent. They are labelled source=agent or source=tool and are not claimed as student understanding. Student-led verification still to be added is listed under planned_student_work and is marked as not yet executed.

user_prompts.content: 请确认你现在使用的是独立的仓库分支，不会收到其他 任务的影响

conversations.content: Read the task page and the public cases on branch 2026-competition-round2. Constraints taken from the text: single process over stdin/stdout, data only in /data, committed data must survive kill -9, data can exceed the memory limit, no SQLite/RocksDB/Faiss, Recall@10 >= 0.95 for filtered and unfiltered queries, memory.peak counts page cache. Chose Go with only the standard library, one append-only log as both redo log and data store, rows read back through mmap.

Checked isolation: the checkout is a standalone clone with its own .git, no other worktrees, nothing stashed. Created local branch minivectordb-dev from the upstream round2 commit so later work does not touch the shared branch. Pushing requires the student's private repository.

Mid-session the upstream branch gained 15 more public cases (commit 9f6df2b). Fast-forwarded and found the expected error names (duplicate_key, dimension_mismatch, unsupported_sql) and the driver directives --restart and --mode ann. Changed the error output to carry these names.

experiments.hypothesis: The public cases pass on the first full implementation.
experiments.output: passed 17, failed 3. sql_comparisons, sql_ordering and sql_bigint failed: CREATE TABLE docs (id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, value BIGINT) -> syntax error near 'value BIGINT)'
experiments.interpretation: The parser listed VALUE (and OFFSET) as reserved words, so a column named value was rejected. MySQL does not reserve VALUE here.
experiments.fix: Removed value and offset from the reserved word list.

experiments.hypothesis: Recovery is correct when the log is cut at any byte.
experiments.output: cut 674 round 0: got rows [1 x [7,7]] [2 x [1,1]] want rows [2 x [1,1]] [4 d [4,4]]
experiments.interpretation: The bug was in the test, not the engine: the helper recorded a snapshot after the uncommitted final transaction, so the expected state wrongly included uncommitted rows. The engine output matched the last committed state.
experiments.fix: Run the uncommitted tail without recording it as an expected state.

experiments.hypothesis: kill -9 at random moments, including during recovery, never loses an acknowledged commit and never leaves a partial statement.
experiments.output: ok: 40 rounds, 4764 committed rows / ok: 40 rounds, 4978 committed rows / ok: 40 rounds, 5329 committed rows / ok: 40 rounds, 4750 committed rows
experiments.interpretation: Passes on macOS. This only tests process kill; the task does not test power loss. It does not replace a run on Linux x86_64.

experiments.hypothesis: An IVF index with nprobe = nlist/4 keeps Recall@10 >= 0.95 at 10k x 128d and is faster than exact search.
experiments.output: exact: write_s 0.721 query_s 0.626 peak_rss_mb 26.1 recall_unfiltered 1.0 recall_filtered 1.0 / ivf: query_s 0.442 recall_unfiltered 0.6092 recall_filtered 1.0
experiments.interpretation: Rejected. On uniform random vectors the IVF lists do not separate neighbours, so 0.61 recall would make the performance run invalid, and the time saved was about 30%. Query time is weighted 40% but an invalid run scores 0.
experiments.fix: ann mode uses IVF only from 200k rows; below that it returns exact results.

experiments.hypothesis: Stopping a distance computation once its partial sum exceeds the current K-th best speeds up exact TopK without changing results.
experiments.output: uniform: query_s 0.257 for 400 queries (about 0.64 s per 1000), recall 1.0 / 1.0; later full run query_s 0.671 / clustered: query_s 0.342, recall 1.0 / 1.0
experiments.interpretation: No measurable gain on uniform data, since the K-th best distance stays close to the average. About 2x on clustered data. Kept because results are identical by construction: every term is non-negative.

planned_student_work.content: Run the Docker image on Linux x86_64 with --memory and cgroup v2, read memory.peak and io.stat, and compare with the macOS RSS numbers in E4.
Check the stdin/stdout framing against the official driver when it is published, and adjust the ready line and error names if they differ.

retrospective.content: Trade-off taken: one log as both WAL and data store means each 100-row batch costs one sequential write and one fdatasync, and there are no page writes. The cost is dead row versions after updates; startup compaction rewrites the log when garbage exceeds 256 MiB and the live data.

limitations: Student understanding and independent verification are not yet evidenced in this record; see completeness_note.
All measurements are from macOS arm64 and are reference only.
The I/O protocol is an assumption until the official driver is released.
